subject.title: fix(twitch): time out Helix user resolution lookups

question: Should Twitch target resolution use an unconditional fixed 10-second cutoff even though slower successful Helix responses will be returned as unresolved?
rationale: Source inspection supports adding a bound, but mock-only evidence cannot establish whether 10 seconds is the correct operational budget for real Twitch and proxy/network conditions.

options.title: Retain 10 seconds after live proof
options.body: Require a real fault-injected Twitch resolver run and a normal successful lookup before accepting the fixed cutoff.

options.title: Choose a different fixed budget
options.body: Adjust the constant to an owner-approved duration and validate both timeout and successful lookup behavior at that boundary.

options.title: Accept the tradeoff now
options.body: Land the current cutoff while explicitly accepting possible false unresolved results on unusually slow networks.

recommendation.title: Retain 10 seconds after live proof
recommendation.body: Require a real fault-injected Twitch resolver run and a normal successful lookup before accepting the fixed cutoff.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this person to prior Twitch channel hardening and the relevant runtime boundary.
